description: Bring rendered output PDF sizes down to roughly the size of the originals (or smaller) without breaking the fidelity comparison. Add a mandatory post-render PDF optimization pass (PyMuPDF object streams + deflate + garbage collection, optionally font subsetting) applied to every engine's output, then regenerate the committed corpus outputs and refresh the README status/size reporting. Root cause is confirmed: Chromium/agent-browser emits ~1.27MB of UNCOMPRESSED PDF object dictionaries with no object streams; a PyMuPDF re-save fixes it ~5x, pixel-identically.
steps: In tools/render.py, add an `optimize_pdf(pdf_path: Path) -> None` step that runs AFTER every engine writes its PDF (engine-independent, so both chromium and weasyprint outputs are compacted). Implementation proven during routing: open with pymupdf, optionally `doc.subset_fonts(verbose=False)` inside a try/except (harmless if it fails), then save in place using `doc.save(tmp, garbage=4, deflate=True, deflate_fonts=True, use_objstms=1, clean=True)` and atomically replace the original (save to a sibling temp file then os.replace, since PyMuPDF cannot save over an open file). Re-validate the result still starts with b'%PDF-' and has the same page_count as before optimization; raise if not.

Guarantee the optimization never alters visual content or geometry: after saving, assert page_count is unchanged and page rectangles/rotation are unchanged. (Routing verified pixmaps are byte-identical at 150 dpi and extracted text is identical, so no content change is expected.) Do NOT rescale, re-raster, or downsample anything - this is a structural recompression only.

Make optimization the default but overridable: add a `--no-optimize` flag to tools/render.py (and thread an `optimize: bool = True` param through render()) so a debugging run can inspect the raw engine output. Default ON.

Verify size reduction on representative reports first: render+optimize primary council_best_students (expect ~1.57MB -> ~300-330KB, near or below the 185KB original class), council_school_rank_in_grade (expect ~5.1MB -> ~1MB), region_kata_jumla (~5.5MB -> ~1.06MB). Record before/after bytes and confirm rendered.pdf still opens and matches page count.

Regenerate the committed outputs for the WHOLE corpus so the size win is real and reviewable: run `make convert` (extract->scaffold->render->tune->render->compare across all 46 reports). This is long-running; if time-constrained, at minimum regenerate all outputs via a render+optimize+compare pass over every catalog entry so every committed output/.../rendered.pdf is the new smaller file and every report.json is refreshed. Use the default engine (chromium) so committed metrics stay comparable to the prior baseline; note that if poppler/fonts could not be installed in FEAT-001, the SSIM/pixel numbers will shift for environmental reasons - document this rather than editing thresholds.

Confirm the fidelity gate did not regress from the size change specifically: for a report rendered both before and after optimization with the SAME engine, the compare metrics (SSIM, pixel delta, text drift, column drift) must be effectively unchanged (optimization is pixel-identical), and no report that previously passed a page may now fail it due to optimization. Record a before/after comparison for at least council_best_students.

Refresh reporting: run `uv run python -m tools.status` to regenerate the README conversion-status table from the new report.json files. Additionally, surface the size improvement so the user can see it - e.g. add a rendered-vs-original byte-size column or a short size summary to tools/status.py output / README (follow the existing status-table generation pattern between the <!-- conversion-status:start/end --> markers; keep it generated, not hand-typed).

Update docs (docs/01-fidelity.md or README 'Rendering engine' / a short note) to state that rendered PDFs are structurally optimized post-render (object streams + deflate + garbage collection) to match reference file sizes, that this is content-preserving (pixel-identical), and that WeasyPrint output is natively small. Keep ruff clean and pytest green.

Add a test asserting the optimization is effective and safe: render one report, and assert the optimized rendered.pdf is dramatically smaller than an un-optimized (--no-optimize) render of the same report while having identical page_count and identical rasterized pixels (compare pymupdf pixmaps at a modest dpi). This test must exercise the real optimize_pdf code path and fail if optimization is removed.
acceptance_criteria: Every committed output/<level>/<key>/rendered.pdf is regenerated and is dramatically smaller than before (target: roughly the size of the corresponding corpus/ original or smaller; the ~1.57MB council-best-students render becomes ~300-330KB against a 185KB original class, and multi-MB renders drop ~5x).
Total committed output PDF size is reduced by roughly 4-5x versus the ~174MB baseline recorded in FEAT-001.

Optimization is content-preserving: for at least council_best_students, rasterized pages are pixel-identical (or SSIM ~1.0) between pre- and post-optimization renders with the same engine, and page count/geometry are unchanged.
No report that previously passed a page's fidelity gate loses that pass due to the optimization step; THRESHOLDS unchanged; corpus/ untouched.
README conversion-status table is regenerated by tools/status.py and reflects the new outputs; a size indicator (rendered vs original) is visible.
New optimization test passes; `uv run pytest` and `uv run ruff check .` are green.
verification: uv run python -m tools.render primary council_best_students --engine chromium
uv run python -c "import os; s=os.path.getsize('output/primary/council-best-students/rendered.pdf'); print(s); assert s < 500000, s"
uv run python -m tools.compare primary council_best_students
findings:
COMPLETED. optimize_pdf() in tools/render.py recompresses every engine's output in place (garbage=4, deflate=True, deflate_fonts=True, use_objstms=1) to a deterministic sibling .tmp then os.replace()s it in, after validating %PDF- magic, unchanged page_count and unchanged per-page (width, height, rotation). Default on; --no-optimize / optimize=False escapes it. Font subsetting and clean=True are deliberately NOT used and the docstring records the measurements: subsetting gains ~2% but can make the following save run for minutes, and clean=True measured ~1.4KB LARGER while running >10min on the 16-page region-shule-nafasi-jumla.

GAP FOUND AND FIXED AFTER THE ORIGINAL PASS: the regeneration in commit f0a91d8 touched only 41 of the 46 committed rendered.pdf files. Five secondary reports still had /ObjStm count == 0, i.e. were never recompressed: secondary/school-results (still at its 12,084,098 B baseline), subject-schools-rank, region-schools-rank-private, region-top-schools, region-subjects-performance. All five have now been optimized in place and each was verified page-count-identical, geometry-identical and PIXEL-IDENTICAL (72dpi PPM rasters compared byte-for-byte): 22,115,466 -> 4,578,587 B (4.83x). school-results 12,084,098 -> 2,570,884 (4.70x); subject-schools-rank 5,355,751 -> 1,006,935 (5.32x); region-schools-rank-private 2,547,129 -> 501,471 (5.08x); region-top-schools 1,525,336 -> 333,554 (4.57x); region-subjects-performance 603,152 -> 165,743 (3.64x).

FINAL CORPUS-WIDE RESULT: all 46 outputs now carry object streams (0 files with ObjStm==0). 181,693,210 -> 35,581,700 bytes = 5.11x reduction, which meets the 4-5x acceptance criterion (the pre-fix state was only 3.42x and would have missed it). Aggregate output is now 2.59x the 13,711,857 B corpus total rather than 13.25x. Honest caveat on the 'same size as the originals or smaller' goal: it is approached, not met, in aggregate - the renders are still ~2.6x the references overall and council-best-students is 316,939 B against a 185,490 B original (1.7x). The remaining delta is real content, not slack: the reference PDFs draw gridlines as shared vector content while the renders carry one absolutely-positioned span per glyph cluster.

DOC CORRECTION: README.md and docs/01-fidelity.md both claimed the pass used 'font subsetting' and 'clean=True'. The code does neither, by design. Both documents were corrected and now carry the real corpus-wide 5.11x figure instead of describing only the single-report case.

FIDELITY UNAFFECTED: THRESHOLDS untouched, corpus/ untouched. All 46 report.json remain status 'wip' - the same pre-existing state as the FEAT-001 baseline, so no report lost a page pass to optimization. The committed outputs were recompressed in place rather than re-rendered, deliberately, so no calibration drift was introduced; that is also why the committed outputs carry no render-meta.json sidecar and compare.py falls back to the historical chromium label. Tests: tests/test_engine.py test_optimization_shrinks_pdf_while_preserving_pixels renders the same report with and without optimization and asserts >2x shrink plus byte-identical rasters, so removing the pass fails the suite. uv run pytest 664 passed / 46 skipped; uv run ruff check . clean.
